rubric.why: A pure liquid has a definite boiling point at a given pressure.
rubric.description: Identifies the boiling behaviour of a pure liquid.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a pure liquid boils at a fixed or constant temperature.

rubric.why: A solution generally boils over a range or at a temperature different from that of a pure liquid.
rubric.description: Identifies the boiling behaviour of a solution.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a solution boils over a range or at a different temperature.

modelAnswer: Compare their boiling behaviour under the same pressure.
A pure liquid boils at a fixed, constant temperature, while a solution generally boils over a range or at a different temperature.

items.followUp: State two characteristic properties of non-metals.

rubric.why: Non-metals are a class of elements.
rubric.how: Award for stating that non-metals are elements.

rubric.why: The defining feature of non-metals is that they do not show the properties of metals.
rubric.description: States the defining distinction from metals.
rubric.how: Award for stating that non-metals lack or do not show metallic properties.

modelAnswer: Non-metals are elements that do not have or show the properties of metals.

items.followUp: Write three differences between Dalton’s atomic theory and Thomson’s atomic model.

rubric.why: Rutherford did not specify fixed electron energy levels, whereas Bohr proposed fixed permitted orbits.
rubric.description: Contrasts electron orbits or energy levels.
rubric.how: Award for correctly contrasting Rutherford’s unspecified orbits with Bohr’s fixed permitted orbits.

rubric.why: Rutherford’s orbiting electrons would radiate energy, while electrons in Bohr’s permitted orbits do not radiate energy.
rubric.description: Contrasts energy radiation in the two models.
rubric.how: Award for giving both sides of the energy-radiation difference.

accept: explained the stability of the atom
rubric.why: Rutherford’s model implied that electrons would spiral into the nucleus, while Bohr’s model explained atomic stability.
rubric.description: Contrasts the models’ explanation of atomic stability.
rubric.how: Award for stating Rutherford’s predicted collapse and Bohr’s explanation of stability.

accept: could not explain the hydrogen line spectrum
rubric.why: Bohr’s model explained the hydrogen line spectrum, which Rutherford’s model could not explain.
rubric.description: Contrasts the models’ explanation of the hydrogen line spectrum.
rubric.how: Award for giving both sides of the spectrum difference.

accept: absorb or emit definite amounts of energy
rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons absorb or emit definite amounts of energy when changing energy levels; Rutherford’s theory did not include these transitions.
rubric.description: States Bohr’s energy-transition idea and contrasts it with Rutherford’s theory.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning definite energy absorption or emission during transitions and the absence of this idea in Rutherford’s theory.

modelAnswer: In Rutherford’s theory, electrons revolve around the nucleus without specified fixed energy levels; in Bohr’s theory, electrons occupy fixed permitted orbits.
Rutherford’s orbiting electrons would radiate energy continuously; electrons in Bohr’s permitted orbits do not radiate energy.
Rutherford’s model suggested that electrons would lose energy and spiral into the nucleus; Bohr’s model explained the stability of the atom.
Rutherford’s theory could not explain the hydrogen line spectrum; Bohr’s theory explained the hydrogen line spectrum.
Rutherford’s theory did not include electron transitions between energy levels; Bohr proposed that electrons absorb or emit definite amounts of energy during these transitions.
